(Houston, Texas) | college = [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]] (2017–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–2022 | team1 = [[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years2 = 2022–2024 | team2 = [[Rostock Seawolves]] | years3 = 2024–2025 | team3 = [[Bàsquet Manresa|Manresa]] | years4 = 2025–present | team4 = [[Virtus Bologna]] | highlights = * [[Basketball Champions League Star Lineup|All-FIBA Champions League Second Team]] ([[2024–25 Basketball Champions League|2025]]) * [[All-Liga ACB Team|All-Liga ACB First Team]] ([[2024–25 ACB season|2025]]) * 2× [[All-Basketball Bundesliga Team|All-Bundesliga First Team]] ([[2022–23 Basketball Bundesliga|2023]], [[2023–24 Basketball Bundesliga|2024]]) * First-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] (2021) * Second-team All-Mountain West (2020) }} '''Derrick Samuel Alston Jr.''' (born September 17, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State Broncos]]. ==Early life== Alston worked as a [[ball boy]] for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]], grabbing rebounds for players during warmups.{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Rachel |title=From NBA ball boy to NBA prospect: The 'remarkable' story of Boise State's Alston Jr. |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-basketball/article240283091.html |website=[[Idaho Statesman]] |accessdate=June 28, 2020 |date=February 15, 2020}} Alston attended [[Strake Jesuit College Preparatory]] in [[Houston]], where he played [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for two years. As a senior, he averaged 14.6 points and 5.1 rebounds per game, earning first-team All-District 19-6A honors.{{cite web |last1=Marrion |first1=Jack |title=Cinco Ranch's Chandler voted District 19-6A basketball MVP |url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/katy/sports/article/Cinco-Ranch-s-Chandler-voted-District-19-6A-9727568.php |website=[[Houston Chronicle]] |accessdate=June 28, 2020 |date=April 18, 2016}} Alston received attention from several [[NCAA Division II]] schools but did not have any [[NCAA Division I]] offers, with some programs suggesting that he complete a [[postgraduate season]]. He was convinced to work his way to a basketball scholarship at [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]] after a junior college coach sent film of Alston to the Bronco's coaching staff.{{cite web |last1=Southorn |first1=Dave |title=How Derrick Alston Jr. built himself up to carry the weight for Boise State |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1607241/2020/02/14/derrick-alston-jr-boise-state-basketball/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 24, 2020 |date=February 14, 2020}} ==College career== Alston was invited to [[Walk-on (sports)|walk on]] to Boise State after impressing the team's coaching staff. When he joined Boise State, he stood 6'9" and weighed 148 pounds. Alston [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first year and reached a weight of 170 pounds by the start of his next season. As a freshman, he averaged 0.6 points per game in limited playing time.{{cite web |last1=Rains |first1=B. J. |title=From skinny walk-on to NBA prospect, Derrick Alston Jr. still 'scratching the surface' for Boise State basketball |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/basketball/from-skinny-walk-on-to-nba-prospect-derrick-alston-jr-still-scratching-the-surface-for/article_0e805038-67ed-5934-ad09-4367a8eaa79c.html |website=[[The Idaho Press-Tribune]] |accessdate=June 28, 2020}} He began earning more minutes during his sophomore season due to his work ethic as well as the departure of [[Chandler Hutchison]] to the NBA. On February 9, 2019, Alston scored a career-high 33 points, shooting 12-of-15 from the field, along with four rebounds and four assists in a 105–57 win over [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]].{{cite web |last1=Rains |first1=B. J. |title=Alston's career-high 33 points leads Broncos to rare 100-point game in blowout of San Jose State |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/basketball/alstons-career-high-33-points-leads-broncos-to-rare-100-point-game-in-blowout-of/article_37735d69-a339-5aa9-bacd-df965f459190.html |website=[[The Idaho Press-Tribune]] |accessdate=June 28, 2020 |date=February 9, 2019}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 13.4 points and 3.9 rebounds per game and was an All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] honorable mention selection. His increase in points per game from the previous season ranked first in school history and second in the nation. Before his junior season, he earned a scholarship to play for Boise State. On December 23, 2019, Alston scored a season-high 32 points to go with six assists in an 85–69 victory over [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]] at the [[Diamond Head Classic]].{{cite web |title=Alston comes within one point of his career high as Boise State beats Portland in Hawaii |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/basketball/alston-comes-within-one-point-of-his-career-high-as-boise-state-beats-portland-in/article_99661d62-ba45-5e3e-97cf-c967c4487e34.html |website=[[The Idaho Press-Tribune]] |accessdate=June 28, 2020 |date=December 23, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 17.3 points, 5.2 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game, earning second-team All-Mountain West accolades.{{cite web |title=Derrick Alston Jr. |url=https://broncosports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/derrick-alston-jr-/7053 |publisher=Boise State University Athletics |accessdate=June 28, 2020}} On April 7, 2020, Alston announced that he would enter the [[2020 NBA draft]], while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Alston to Enter 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://broncosports.com/news/2020/3/30/mens-basketball-alston-to-enter-2020-nba-draft.aspx |publisher=Boise State University Athletics |accessdate=June 28, 2020 |date=March 30, 2020}} On July 8, Alston announced that he would be returning to Boise State for his final season.{{cite news |last1=Kloppenburg |first1=Katie |title=Derrick Alston, Jr. returning for senior year at Boise State |url=https://www.kivitv.com/news/derrick-alston-jr-returning-for-senior-year-at-boise-state |accessdate=August 4, 2020 |work=KIVITV |date=July 8, 2020}} ==Professional career== [[File: Alston Jr 2024.jpg|thumb|180px|Alston with [[Bàsquet Manresa|Manresa]] in 2024]] After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Alston joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Isabel|last=Gonzalez|title=Derrick Alston Jr. set to join Golden State Summer League team|url=https://mwwire.com/2021/07/31/derrick-alston-jr-set-to-play-summer-league-with-golden-state/|website=Mountain West Wire|date=July 31, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} On September 13, 2021, he signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Jazz Sign Derrick Alston Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-derrick-alston-jr|website=NBA.com|date=September 13, 2021|access-date=September 14, 2021}} He was waived prior to the start of the season. In October 2021, Alston joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web |title=Training Camp Roster Finalized |url=https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/stars-finalize-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 1, 2021 |date=October 25, 2021 |archive-date=November 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102002429/https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/stars-finalize-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }} Alston joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612742/mavericks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On August 15, 2022, he has signed with [[Rostock Seawolves]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/derrick-alston-jr-joins-rostock-seawolves/|title=Derrick Alston Jr joins Rostock Seawolves|last=|first=|date=August 15, 2022|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 17, 2022}} On January 28, 2023, Alston's [[NBA G League]] rights were traded from the [[Iowa Wolves]] to the [[Long Island Nets]] in exchange for [[Craig Randall II]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 28, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2023}} Alston joined [[Bàsquet Manresa|Manresa]] of the [[Liga ACB]] in July 2024, signing a one year deal. His father [[Derrick Alston]] played for the Catalans in the [[1997–98 ACB season]], in which [[Bàsquet Manresa]] won its first and only [[List of Spanish basketball champions|Liga ACB trophy]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basquetmanresa.com/noticies/equips/noticies/2024/el-baxi-manresa-fitxa-derrick-alston-jr-fill-del-mitic-campio-del-98/|title=El BAXI Manresa fitxa Derrick Alston Jr, fill del mític campió del '98|website=basquetmanresa.com|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=December 1, 2024|lang=ca}} With Manresa, Alston won the [[ACB Player of the Month Award]] in January 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/494176-derrick-alston-jr-mvp-movistar-del-mes-de-enero.html |title=Derrick Alston Jr., MVP Movistar del mes de enero |website=acb.com|date=January 26, 2025|access-date=January 28, 2025|lang=es}} Alston was named to the [[All-Liga ACB Team|All-Liga ACB First Team]] for the [[2024-25 ACB season]].{{cite news |title=Mejor Quinteto de la Liga Endesa 2024-25 |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/511770-mejor-quinteto-de-la-liga-endesa-202425.html |access-date=27 May 2025 |work=www.acb.com |date=27 May 2025 |language=es}} In June 2025, he signed with [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=2025-06-28 |title=Virtus adds forward Derrick Alston Jr.
